code.source:
import random
random.seed(4)
secret = random.randint(1, 10)
tries = 0
while True:
    guess = int(input("Guess 1-10: "))
    tries = tries + 1
    if guess < secret:
        print("Too low")
    elif guess > secret:
        print("Too high")
    else:
        print("Correct in", tries, "tries")
        break

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: comparing text with a number
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the Python error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. We compare the guess with the secret, but the guess is still text. Python says, type error. Greater than is not supported between a string and an int. Remember, input always gives text. Wrap the answer in int, and now both sides are numbers. Then the comparison works.

shorts.title: The game plan
shorts.script: Let us build a game. The computer picks a secret number. The player guesses. The program says Too low or Too high, until the guess is right. You need a loop that repeats, decisions with if and else, and a counter for the tries. Everything from this module comes together. Plan the flow on paper first. Then the code is easy to write. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Our first project.

shorts.title: Random numbers
shorts.hook: "To pick a secret number, import the random tool."
shorts.script: To pick a secret number, import the random tool. Then random dot randint, one comma ten, gives a whole number from one to ten, and both ends are included. Set a seed first, and the same number comes up every run, which is great for testing. Remove the seed line, and the number changes every time, just like a real game. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Pick a secret.

shorts.title: While true
shorts.script: The game loop is while True. That means, loop forever, until we say stop. Inside, we ask for a guess, compare it, and print a hint. When the guess is right, we print the result and use break. Break is the only way out. This pattern, loop forever and break when done, is very common in games and menus. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Loop until you win.

shorts.title: Text versus number
shorts.hook: "Here is the bug that breaks every first guessing game."
shorts.script: Here is the bug that breaks every first guessing game. You compare the guess with the secret, but the guess came from input, so it is text. Python says type error, greater than is not supported between a string and an int. Wrap the input in int, and both sides are numbers. Now the comparison works as you expect. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Convert with int.

shorts.hook: "Why did the guessing game never get lonely?"
shorts.script: Why did the guessing game never get lonely? It always had a number in mind. Your challenge. Make the game fairer. Let the player lose after five wrong guesses. When that happens, print the secret number, and stop the loop. You can use the tries counter you already have. Share your improved game in the comments below. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
